records.notes: FR-040 boundary class for `build`: an image-reference configuration whose collection fields are all present and empty. An empty `features` map is the specific edge — it must produce the base image unchanged rather than an empty Feature layer or a failure.

Replaces the `--cache-to` half of `parity_build::buildkit-only-features` (res-build-tolerant-outcome). What this establishes is bounded and worth stating: deacon accepts the flag, passes it through, and still produces the image. What it does NOT establish is that anything was cached. The export type is `inline` on purpose: it is the ONE type buildx's default `docker` driver supports across Docker versions, so the case measures deacon rather than the runner. It was `type=local,dest=…` and that was the environment-dependent part — cache export needs the `docker-container` driver on older Docker, so on a CI runner the build produced no image at all and the case failed for a reason that had nothing to do with deacon (measured: it passes on Docker 29.6.2 / BuildKit v0.31.2, fails on GitHub `ubuntu-latest`, and Podman has no equivalent). Local export was never the claim either — even where it succeeded it wrote nothing to the destination. Pinning the reachable claim and naming the unreachable one is the honest shape; the legacy unit instead tolerated failure and, in its failure arm, accepted any of three substrings one of which (`outcome`) appears in normal JSON success output, so it could not fail either way.

Closes the Compose half of #440. The Compose build shape produces its feature-extended image through `resolve_compose_feature_image` rather than the Dockerfile path, and for that reason was outside #436's fix: it stamped no `devcontainer.metadata` at all, so an image a Compose `build` produced told a later `up` (or VS Code / Zed / envbuilder) nothing about the Features installed in it. The label is pinned WHOLE and by value rather than by presence: the entries are ordered (each installed Feature, then the config pick, lowest precedence first), and a presence check would pass on a label that recorded the wrong thing or dropped the Feature. `source: image` is pinned because a `build` leaves no container, so evidence captured from one would be answering a different question. Image pinned to alpine:3.19.

Covers the high-risk triple `hrt-build-compose-no-features-structured`. Building a Compose configuration has to resolve the SERVICE's build shape rather than the top-level one; the `-app` suffix on the reported image name is what shows which of the two was read, and `outcome` alone would not — a build of the wrong thing succeeds too. The image name's leading segment carries a workspace-derived hash and is deliberately left unpinned. Spec-expectation rather than differential because the structured rendering is reached by a flag the two CLIs spell differently, and the runner sends one argv to both sides.

The alignment half of the Dockerfile-plus-Feature build: both CLIs complete the build and report success. Kept separate from the `--image-name` case because the two CLIs do not share a tagging flag surface, so the overlay half cannot be a differential.

Covers the high-risk triple `hrt-build-dockerfile-cli-overlay-single-feature`. A Dockerfile build, a Feature layered on top of it, and a user-supplied `--image-name` — the exact combination in which this project once shipped a tag pointing at the PRE-Feature base. The assertion pins both halves in one ordered match: the reported image is the FEATURE-EXTENDED one (`deacon-devcontainer-features:…`), and the user's tag is among the tags applied to it. The stronger observation — running the tag and reading the Feature's marker — needs a `docker run` the declarative runner does not model, so the ordering constraint stands in for it and this note records the difference.

FR-034 build-time failure: the Dockerfile's `RUN` exits non-zero, so no image is produced. Both CLIs must fail, and the declared phase records WHERE — a build failure and a container-creation failure are the same exit code and different facts, which is the whole reason the phase is part of the record.

allowedDifferences.rationale: deacon stamps `org.deacon.configHash` on the image it builds; the reference sets no such label (measured against the pinned oracle 0.87.0 on this fixture). One named key in deacon's own namespace, never the `org.deacon.*` namespace as a whole. `devcontainer.metadata` is deliberately NOT tolerated alongside it: it was a deacon defect (#436), it is fixed, and the two sides now agree on that key — so a regression reappears here as a divergence instead of being excused.

records.notes: Ports `parity_build::with-build-args` (res-build-image-discovery). The fixture routes one `build.args` value into BOTH an image label and an environment variable, and the Dockerfile's `ARG` default is `default-not-passed` — so a build that silently dropped `build.args` produces an image that still exists and still carries the label, and is caught here by the VALUE (`default-not-passed` instead of `passed-from-config`) on two independent observables. That is the failure the legacy unit's substring check over `docker inspect` output was reaching for; this compares the whole image configuration between the CLIs instead. Everything agrees except `org.deacon.configHash`, which is tolerated (a deacon extension). `devcontainer.metadata` is NOT tolerated: deacon used to write it here unconditionally (a placeholder carrying `configHash`) where the reference writes it only when there is metadata to carry, and this fixture declares no Features and nothing in the configuration pick — so the defect showed up as a one-sided key. #436 closed it and neither side writes the label on this fixture now. Image pinned to alpine:3.19 (V18).

records.notes: Ports `parity_build::creates-discoverable-image` (res-build-image-discovery) and strengthens it. The legacy unit asked only whether an image carrying a unique label EXISTED after each side's build — a question answerable by a build that produced the wrong image entirely, as long as the label came along. This compares the produced image's whole configuration between the two CLIs: labels, environment, command, entrypoint, working directory. Made observable by the built-image capability: a `build` leaves an image and no container, so the container probe sees nothing and the case passes `--image-name ${IMAGE_TAG}` for a runner-assigned, per-side tag the observer inspects and the workspace reclaims. The image's own IDENTITY is not compared — the two sides build separately into different tags, so id/digests/tags differ by construction and say nothing about behavior. The label is a fixed literal rather than the legacy unit's PID-uniquified token: discovery is now by the assigned tag, so global uniqueness across concurrent runs is no longer the case's problem. TWO label keys once differed and are treated differently on purpose — `org.deacon.configHash` is a deacon extension and is tolerated by one named key; `devcontainer.metadata` was a deacon defect (#436) and is NOT tolerated, so this case reported it until the fix landed and reports any regression the same way. Image pinned to alpine:3.19 (V18).

Ports `parity_build::image-reference` (res-build-image-discovery), which is DEACON-ONLY — it never invoked the oracle — so a spec-expectation is its honest shape; a live-differential would claim cross-CLI agreement the unit never checked. Building from a plain image reference with a user tag and a `--label`, it pins the two halves the legacy unit checked and one it could not. (1) The reported `imageName` contains the tag the user asked for, asserted through the `<IMAGE_TAG>` token — the runner assigns a per-run, per-side tag, so the literal is unassertable and the token is what makes the claim expressible at all. (2) The produced IMAGE carries the `--label` value: the legacy unit inferred this from `docker images --filter label=…` returning a non-empty list, which proves only that SOME image matched; this reads the label off the image the build was told to write. `source: image` is pinned deliberately — without it the assertion would also pass on evidence captured from a container, and the whole point of this case is that a `build` leaves no container to capture.

Replaces `parity_build::output-json-format` (res-build-tolerant-outcome) by PINNING the outcome instead of porting the tolerance. The legacy unit branched on success/failure and, in its failure arm, accepted stdout or stderr containing any of "BuildKit is required", "outcome" or "Docker" — and a `--output-format json` build prints `outcome` in its normal success output, so the failure arm could pass on almost anything. An assertion that cannot fail is worse than no assertion. `--output type=docker,dest=…` is deterministic wherever a build can run at all: it exports to a path the case owns, so there is a single correct outcome to pin. The claim is deliberately the ARTIFACT, not the echo — `exportPath` alone repeats the flag back and would pass on a build that wrote nothing, so `chan-filesystem` asserts the tar exists. `<WORKSPACE>` is the path token; the case writes inside its own isolated workspace, which the runner reclaims. Image pinned to alpine:3.19 (V18).

Closes the `--output` half of #440, and is deacon-only (`--output` has no reference counterpart), so a spec-expectation is its honest shape. A `--push`/`--output` build used to hand its export straight to BuildKit, which left no local image to stamp — the exported image therefore carried NO `devcontainer.metadata`, having previously carried a wrong one. deacon now builds into the daemon, stamps, and exports from there, which is what makes the label observable at all: the export pass also loads, so the tag the case assigns names the STAMPED image and `chan-image` can read the label off it. `chan-filesystem` keeps the artifact claim from `case-build-output-export-tar` — a stamped image that was never exported would satisfy the label assertion alone. Image pinned to alpine:3.19.

Replaces the `--platform` half of `parity_build::buildkit-only-features` (res-build-tolerant-outcome). The legacy unit tolerated either outcome on the theory that BuildKit might be absent; it then asserted, only in the failure arm, that some error string appeared — so on any machine WITH BuildKit (every machine this suite runs on, and the default since Docker 23) it asserted nothing at all. `--platform` on the host's own architecture is deterministic, so this pins success and, through `chan-image`, that the flag produced a real image carrying the Dockerfile's label rather than merely being accepted. A genuinely BuildKit-less environment now fails this case loudly, which is the correct report — the suite's prerequisites are checked, not guessed at. Image pinned to alpine:3.19 (V18).

Replaces `parity_build::push-json-output` (res-build-tolerant-outcome). The legacy unit pushed to `localhost:5000` and branched on whether that happened to be reachable, so its assertion depended on the machine. `registry.invalid` is RFC 2606 reserved and resolves nowhere, so the push ALWAYS fails and there is one outcome to pin: exit 1, and a diagnostic that names the push as the failing step AND the target it failed on. Naming the target is what makes this case observe `bhv-build-push-target-selection` rather than merely assert it: deacon used to hand the push to BuildKit, which pushed every `-t` tag including deacon's internal `deacon-build:<hash>` — no registry component, so Docker Hub — and that push failed FIRST, so the reported target was the wrong one (#438). Restructuring the publish step for #440 made the push deacon's own and scoped it to the image names the user supplied, so the message now names `registry.invalid/conformance-push:latest`. The quoted target is deacon's own wording; the daemon's reason for the failure is BuildKit/daemon phrasing and is deliberately not pinned. Image pinned to alpine:3.19 (V18).

A `features` value written as a bare string rather than an object, on `build`. This case carried a tolerance excusing an exit-code difference on the premise that "the reference accepts it and builds"; that premise is FALSE at oracle 0.87.0 and the tolerance was reported STALE the moment stale tolerances began failing. Re-measured: both CLIs exit 1. They reject for different reasons — deacon fails at config parse (`expected an object (map), found a string`), while the reference indexes the string as a legacy character-keyed feature map and fails with `Legacy feature '0' not supported` — but the observable exit code agrees, so there is nothing left to excuse and the class is `malformed`, not `reference-lenient`. The reference's LENIENCY toward this input is real on `read-configuration`, where it echoes the config instead of rejecting it; that is where `bhv-readconfig-wrong-type-features-rejected` and `wvr-wrong-type-features` still apply, and `case-errors-decl-wrong-type-features` pins the direction. Image pinned to alpine:3.18 (V18).

FR-040 unsupported class for `build`: a well-formed configuration naming an image reference no registry serves. Nothing about the document is wrong; the failure can only appear once something tries to obtain the image.

allowedDifferences.rationale: deacon stamps `org.deacon.configHash` on the image it builds; the reference sets no such label. Identical in scope and reasoning to the tolerance every other `chan-image` case in this suite carries — one named key in deacon's own namespace, never the `org.deacon.*` namespace as a whole — and re-measured against oracle 0.87.0 on this fixture. No other image key is tolerated here, so a regression on any of them surfaces as a divergence rather than being excused.

records.notes:
A Dockerfile whose first line is a `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1` frontend directive, with an `ARG` consumed by `FROM` beneath it. The directive is meaningful only to BuildKit and only when it is the FIRST line — a CLI that rewrites, prepends to, or re-emits the Dockerfile (to inject Feature layers, or to resolve the `ARG`) can displace it, at which point Docker reads it as an ordinary comment and the build silently falls back to the classic frontend. The produced image is compared whole, so a frontend swap that changes anything observable about the image surfaces here.

MEASURED at oracle 0.87.0: the two images agree on everything except deacon's `org.deacon.configHash`, which is the extension every `chan-image` case in this suite already tolerates.

The fixture carries one authored `LABEL` for a reason worth recording. Without it the reference's image has NO labels at all (`Config.Labels` is `null`) while deacon's has its bookkeeping key, so the sides differ at the `labels` NODE rather than at a key inside it — the case's key-scoped tolerance could not reach it, and the run reported a STALE tolerance instead of a tolerated difference. A tolerance scoped to `<map>.<key>` is unreachable whenever the other side's whole map is absent.

records.notes:
RED AND EXPECTED — a deacon-side divergence. `build.target` and `build.options` together, on a Dockerfile written to catch a wrong answer: three stages, a decoy BEFORE the named target and a decoy AFTER it, so an implementation that builds the last stage and one that builds the first both produce a DIFFERENT image rather than a failure.

MEASURED at oracle 0.87.0. `build.target` AGREES — `/var/test-marker` carries `||test-content||` in both images, so both built the middle stage and skipped both decoys. `build.options` does NOT: the reference's image carries `test_build_options=success`, deacon's carries no such label, so the `--label test_build_options=success` the configuration asked to be passed through to the builder never reached it. Diverging path: `chan-image.labels.test_build_options`.

`devcontainerjson-reference.md` defines `build.options` as "an array of Docker CLI build options" the tool passes to the build, so this is a modelled property deacon accepts, echoes in `read-configuration`, and then ignores — the silent-fallback shape constitution IV rules out. Left red for triage; the ONE tolerance the case carries is the bookkeeping label every other `chan-image` case tolerates, and it is deliberately not widened to cover this.

Mined from the reference CLI's own e2e fixtures (#480, batch 1). Vendored from devcontainers/cli v0.87.0; see the fixture's UPSTREAM.md for the source path and every adaptation.

Error-path tier, build stage, with the build ARGUMENT as the thing under test. The Dockerfile's `RUN` exits non-zero only when `CONF_FAIL=1` reaches it, and the configuration is the only place that value comes from — so a CLI that dropped `build.args` would SUCCEED here. The failure is therefore evidence that the argument was delivered, which the ordinary build-args case (`case-tier1-build-args-subst`, a configuration comparison) cannot supply: it observes the resolved document, not what the builder received. Both sides fail (verified against oracle 0.87.0).

Error-path tier, build stage: `build.target` names a stage the Dockerfile does not define. Nothing about the document is wrong and BOTH CLIs read it without complaint — the target is a free-form string, and no reader can know which stages exist until the builder resolves the Dockerfile graph. That is the point: the failure is unreachable until after the stage where the reference is most lenient, which is exactly where parity used to stop comparing. Both sides fail (verified against oracle 0.87.0 in an isolated workspace).
